answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it may submit bids or vote. When independent reviewers prove that accounts coordinated to claim rewards as separate agents, the protocol confiscates their deposits and divides the bounty among reporters. Splitting one operator across a delta of accounts therefore multiplies the capital at risk, while a new island of identities cannot earn trust merely by appearing. A quill-thin stake is insufficient if voting weight is capped by collateral.
